issues.reason: announcer passes both agent-nominalization tests (announce stands alone as a verb; "an announcer is one who announces" is true by definition) and is the copular predicate of its clause, and the section states the firing sites are "fixed, not a judgment call" precisely so two faithful parses cannot differ — so (Inheritance announcer (can announce)) is required, not optional.

gaps_confirmed: equative / specificational copula with a definite predicate nominal ("David Ross was THE announcer"): Categorical statements covers only "X is a/an N" and "X is ADJ", so the uniqueness of the role is not representable and the clause can only fall back on plain class membership
new_gaps: the agent-nominalization copular-predicate trigger is glossed as firing "where the sentence is about what the kind is" and is illustrated only with a kind subject ("Penguins are swimmers"); nothing says whether an INDIVIDUAL subject with a definite predicate nominal (a role-identifying equative) still counts as a predicative use or as the referring use that stops at typing

the tense treatment of a definitional capability atom yielded by a past-tense copular clause is unstated — the mechanical wrapper rule says a past copular wraps every categorical atom the clause yields, while the "Penguins are swimmers" example shows the capability atom keeping its own definitional (STV 1.0 0.99) independent of the host clause
repair_summary: Added the required agent-nominalization capability atom (: tc341_announcer_can (Inheritance announcer (can announce)) (STV 1.0 0.99)) directly after the clause it comes from, unwrapped and at the definitional TV the "Penguins are swimmers" example gives it; nothing else changed.
notes: No object is incorporated in announcer, so no kind-relation atom accompanies the capability. The two clauses being translated independently with no atom for coordinating "and", Theme on the unchanged orchestra, and the single Name atom per proper noun are all correct.
